answer: Running 132 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the sparrow schedule in the tide ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the dawn checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 6 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 24 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
